title: Remainders Game
statementMd:
Today Pari and Arya are playing a game called Remainders.

Pari chooses two positive integer $*x*$ and $*k*$, and tells Arya $*k*$ but not $*x*$. Arya have to find the value ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/fddd3bb34fa9f786754485afa55927f021d74d15.png). There are $*n*$ ancient numbers $*c*_{1}, *c*_{2}, ..., *c*_{*n*}$ and Pari has to tell Arya ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/fbb55ab61f79d427b1a3d23470b55aa433de55e7.png) if Arya wants. Given $*k*$ and the ancient values, tell us if Arya has a winning strategy independent of value of $*x*$ or not. Formally, is it true that Arya can understand the value ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/fddd3bb34fa9f786754485afa55927f021d74d15.png) for any positive integer $*x*$?

Note, that ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/f58f159973d4609d919286c1821e69cd34d81118.png) means the remainder of $*x*$ after dividing it by $*y*$.

## Input

The first line of the input contains two integers $*n*$ and $*k*$ ($1 ≤ *n*,  *k* ≤ 1 000 000$) — the number of ancient integers and value $*k*$ that is chosen by Pari.

The second line contains $*n*$ integers $*c*_{1}, *c*_{2}, ..., *c*_{*n*}$ ($1 ≤ *c*_{*i*} ≤ 1 000 000$).

## Output

Print "`Yes`" (without quotes) if Arya has a winning strategy independent of value of $*x*$, or "`No`" (without quotes) otherwise.

## Note

In the first sample, Arya can understand ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/d170efffcde0907ee6bcf32de21051bce0677a2c.png) because $5$ is one of the ancient numbers.

In the second sample, Arya can't be sure what ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/57b5f6a96f5db073270dd3ed4266c69299ec701d.png) is. For example $1$ and $7$ have the same remainders after dividing by $2$ and $3$, but they differ in remainders after dividing by $7$.
